definitions.definition: When a tiny particle's many possible states suddenly become just one real state after you measure it.
definitions.example: Like a spinning coin that is both heads and tails until you slap it down and it becomes only heads.

definitions.definition: A perfect one-to-one match between two things where every part of one has a matching part in the other.
definitions.example: Like a map of a subway system that matches the real tracks exactly, station for station.

definitions.definition: A state where a particle exists in all possible states at once until it is measured.
definitions.example: Like a coin spinning in the air that is both heads and tails at the same time.

definitions.definition: A single definite state that a particle settles into after being measured.
definitions.example: Like the coin finally landing on heads and staying that way.

definitions.definition: Happening in an instant, with no time passing at all.
definitions.example: Like flipping a light switch — the light is off one moment and on the next, with no in-between.

definitions.definition: Cannot be undone or reversed.
definitions.example: Like cracking an egg — you can't put it back together again.

definitions.definition: Affecting things that are far apart instantly, as if distance doesn't matter.
definitions.example: Like two magic coins that always show the same side even if one is on Earth and the other on Mars.

definitions.definition: When two particles are linked so that measuring one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart they are.
definitions.example: Like a pair of magic dice that always show the same number when rolled, even across the room.

definitions.definition: The idea that one person's action counts for everyone they represent.
definitions.example: Like a team captain signing a contract that binds the whole team.

definitions.definition: A complete shift in the rules or nature of a system, not just a small change.
definitions.example: Like going from playing checkers to playing chess — the pieces and moves are totally different.

definitions.definition: A type of smooth, predictable change in a quantum system that can be reversed.
definitions.example: Like a perfectly smooth pendulum swing that you could run backward.

definitions.definition: When the future is completely set by the past, with no randomness.
definitions.example: Like a clock — if you know how it's set, you know exactly what time it will show later.

definitions.definition: A formula that tells you the chance of getting each possible result when you measure a quantum particle.
definitions.example: Like knowing that a fair coin has a 50% chance of heads and 50% chance of tails.

definitions.definition: The number of independent ways a system can change or be in different states.
definitions.example: Like a ball on a table can move left-right and forward-back — that's two degrees of freedom.

definitions.definition: A math rule that describes how quantum particles change smoothly over time when not being measured.
definitions.example: Like a recipe that tells you how a wave in a pond will spread out.

definitions.definition: When you observe or measure a quantum particle, causing it to pick one definite state.
definitions.example: Like opening a box to see if a cat is alive or dead — the act of looking forces a result.

definitions.definition: The specific value you get when you measure a quantum property, like a particle's position or speed.
definitions.example: Like the exact number on a scale when you weigh yourself.

definitions.definition: The basic underlying stuff or layer that everything else is built on.
definitions.example: Like the foundation of a house that supports the walls and roof.

definitions.definition: Visible or clear forms that something takes when it appears in the real world.
definitions.example: Like steam, water, and ice are all manifestations of H2O.

definitions.definition: Able to be proven wrong by evidence or testing.
definitions.example: Like saying 'all swans are white' can be proven false by finding one black swan.

definitions.definition: A perfect one-to-one pairing where each thing in one group matches exactly one thing in another group, with nothing left over.
definitions.example: Like assigning each student in a class a unique locker number — every student gets one locker, and every locker has one student.

definitions.definition: A proven idea that says quantum particles can be linked in ways that are faster than light and not explained by normal physics.
definitions.example: Like a proof that magic coins that always match can't be explained by hidden tricks — they must be truly linked.

definitions.definition: A standard way of understanding quantum mechanics that says particles don't have definite properties until they are measured.
definitions.example: Like saying a cat in a box is both alive and dead until you open it — that's the Copenhagen view.

definitions.definition: Something that keeps a quantum system in a smooth, wave-like state and prevents it from collapsing into one definite state.
definitions.example: Like a perfect gyroscope that keeps spinning without wobbling, resisting any force that would stop it.

definitions.definition: Something that causes a quantum system to lose its wave-like behavior and act like a normal, definite object.
definitions.example: Like air resistance that slows a spinning top until it falls over and stops.

definitions.definition: A Hebrew word (pronounced vai-yip-pa-ke-chu) meaning 'and they were opened' — used in Genesis 3:7 for the instant their eyes opened.
definitions.example: Like saying 'click' for a light turning on — it's a sudden, not gradual, action.
